chapters.title: Module 1 – Using language to talk about locations, emergency help and volunteering

lessons.title: Situation 1: Locating and using the services of agencies that provide emergency help (revision of problem areas)
Situation 2: Using simple maps to locate places (WH questions)
Situation 3: Reporting an emergency outside the home (prepositions of place and direction)
Situation 4: Getting involved or volunteering in solving community problems (polite forms)

chapters.title: Module 2 – Using language to explain procedures used to purchase goods and services

lessons.title: Situation 1: Comparing methods of purchasing, including catalogues and online purchasing (comparatives)
Situation 2: Writing a cheque (gerunds)
Situation 3: Responding to a cashier's questions about means of payment (expressions of purpose)
Situation 4: Consumer protection resources against fraudulent practices (subordination)

chapters.title: Module 3 – Using language to explore safety measures and health risks

lessons.title: Situation 1: Handling, preparing and storing food safely (relative clauses)
Situation 2: Problems related to drugs, tobacco and alcohol, and where to get treatment (direct and indirect speech)
Situation 3: Interpreting procedures for simple first aid (first and second conditionals)
Situation 4: Safety signs and measures that prevent accidents and injuries (present perfect and present perfect continuous)

chapters.title: Module 4 – Using language to examine civic and legal rights, responsibilities and infractions

lessons.title: Situation 1: Legal and civic rights and responsibilities: voting, taxes, national emblems (phrasal verbs)
Situation 2: Legal rights and obligations in domestic relationships (word order in expressions of purpose)
Situation 3: Common infractions and their legal consequences (structures with adjectives)
Situation 4: Procedures for reporting problems and crimes (modals of obligation)

chapters.title: Module 5 – Using language to explore safe and responsible use of ICTs

lessons.title: Situation 1: Finding out about and coping with cyberbullying
Situation 2: Distinguishing fact from opinion and fiction from non-fiction in social media
Situation 3: Detecting cyber criminality: scamming and hacking
Writing expository essays on cyber criminality (revising verb tenses)
